reason: The cited evidence shows that ML potentials can accelerate DFT-level sampling (E1, E2) and that simulation-based entropy methods work for high-entropy alloys (E3), but none of the passages provides specific prior evidence that ML potentials accurately capture anharmonicity and electron-vibration coupling in free-energy calculations, nor that active learning combined with free-energy integration achieves the claimed speedup for multicomponent systems.
premises: ML potentials can serve as fast, accurate surrogates for DFT potential energy surfaces
Active learning can efficiently calibrate ML potentials with minimal AIMD data
ML potentials can capture vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron-vibration coupling
Free-energy integration methods (e.g., TOR-TILD) can be combined with ML potentials
The approach reduces computational cost by at least one order of magnitude vs. explicit AIMD/TOR-TILD
